entries.notes: The bootstrap exposes semantic heading and main landmarks without unapproved business actions.
Non-production context and a public immutable build identifier are visible in the support area.
Production omits the environment indicator while retaining the public build identifier.
A real isolated PostgreSQL database upgrades from empty to the single reviewed head.
The runtime role can read the baseline but cannot issue schema DDL.
Injected transactional DDL failure preserves the prior revision and baseline without reset or recreation.
The additive baseline check rejects malformed input while preserving valid history.
A current-head no-op migration completes within the bounded baseline expectation while a reader is open.
Versioned minimal liveness response includes a generated correlation identifier.
Readiness returns only a stable success status after the runtime database accepts the check.
Missing runtime database configuration produces the same minimal unavailable response as a failed check.
Runtime database check failures make the API not ready without exposing failure details.
Both readiness outcomes preserve the safe caller correlation identifier.
Readiness failures never return SQL, URLs, credentials, paths, hosts, identities, or exception text.
The repository-managed PostgreSQL gate proves readiness through the runtime identity and managed runtime URL.
Safe caller identifiers are trimmed and returned on the response.
Unsafe, empty, or over-length caller header values are replaced with generated identifiers.
Non-ASCII caller identifiers are rejected at the normalization boundary.
Operational liveness is exposed only below the canonical API base path, and correlation is preserved on a 404 response.
The unauthenticated liveness body remains minimal and excludes process secrets.
Unknown routes return the canonical 404 envelope with correlated request ID and no requested object disclosure.
HTTP exception details are replaced by stable safe status-specific content.
Every canonical HTTP error status has an exact stable envelope and request-ID correlation.
Request validation exposes only bounded field locations, never rejected values or framework diagnostics.
Malformed JSON returns the exact correlated safe 400 envelope without parser diagnostics or rejected request content.
Unexpected failures return a correlated canonical 500 without exception, SQL, credential, path, or object details.
Application request logs are structured and request-ID correlated while omitting paths, query values, headers, credentials, tokens, and bodies.
Unexpected failures emit correlated operational diagnostics limited to the exception type and never exception text, stack traces, paths, Customer data, or financial data.
The JSON formatter enforces a fixed operational-field allowlist and ignores message text and arbitrary extras that could contain sensitive payloads.
FastAPI lifespan enters application-owned asynchronous resources and closes them during graceful shutdown with structured lifecycle events.
A non-secret immutable build identity is loaded from deployment configuration.
Application settings read only the runtime database URL and retain it as a secret value.
Without an injected provider-established actor, the protected identity seam denies server-side with the canonical correlated 401 envelope.
The provider-neutral default does not alter the public minimal liveness contract.

An injected request-to-actor provider can establish one stable opaque actor identifier and the endpoint-required identity.read_self capability with exact self-object scope; the API core returns only the identifier in the canonical correlated resource envelope.
An authenticated actor with no provider-established capability grant receives the canonical 403 response rather than inheriting authority.
The reusable server authorization primitive rejects a matching capability whose trusted Property scope does not exactly contain the operation's Property.
The identity endpoint returns 403 when its required capability is scoped to a different exact actor object.
Role, capability, Property, and object headers remain untrusted; an authenticated actor without provider grants receives 403 and no role name is interpreted by the API core.
Authorization, actor, capability, role, Property, and object headers are inert when no trusted external provider is injected, so client assertions cannot establish identity or authority.
The single Property's business date changes exactly at the Asia/Phnom_Penh local calendar boundary.
A timezone-aware instant is normalized to the authoritative Property timezone before its business date is derived.
An instant without explicit timezone semantics is rejected rather than silently interpreted as a business date.
The identity scope accepts an object assigned to the one Property managed by the application.
The identity scope rejects an object whose authoritative Property ID differs from the application's single Property ID.

The real PostgreSQL schema stores UUID actor identity, normalized username, display and audit identity, lifecycle and MFA-policy classes, timestamps, and provenance without credential, role, capability, MFA-verifier, recovery, or session columns.
PostgreSQL rejects a committed duplicate normalized username through a transactional unique constraint.
The account table rejects usernames that are not trimmed, lowercase normalized values.
A PostgreSQL trigger prevents mutation of an established UUID actor identity.
The account lifecycle is explicit and rejects values outside active or disabled.
MFA policy is stored as required or optional rather than as a role or capability grant.
Display identity, audit identity, and creation provenance cannot be blank.
The runtime identity can read account identity data but has no insert, update, delete, truncate, or column-write privilege before audited account operations exist.
PostgreSQL initializes account timestamps together and advances the managed update timestamp on change.
A real PostgreSQL database advances from the prior reviewed revision to the account-storage head while retaining baseline data.
The real PostgreSQL schema contains only the linked adaptive verifier encoding, algorithm/work-factor metadata, lifecycle timestamps, and audit provenance required by the bounded credential tranche.
PostgreSQL rejects plaintext-shaped or mismatched verifier encodings, invalid algorithms, non-positive/non-integral work-factor metadata, and blank audit provenance.
The runtime identity can read only verifier-checking columns and has no table-level read or write privilege and no access to audit provenance.
A credential row cannot exist without its immutable local-account actor identity.
A credential-material change preserves creation time, advances managed change time, and records the responsible actor and new audit provenance.
Credential updates reject missing responsible actors, stale provenance, and audit-only mutation without changed verifier material.
The prior account migration continues to refuse destructive downgrade in an isolated real PostgreSQL database.
The credential migration refuses destructive downgrade and leaves the credential table and Alembic history at the reviewed head.
A real PostgreSQL database advances from the account-storage revision to credential storage while preserving an existing account row.
The routed credential-storage, testing, security, and approved-decision identifiers remain mapped to implemented focused tests.
The service produces distinct Argon2id encodings for the same password with explicit current adaptive work-factor metadata and no plaintext persistence.
A correct password verifies against current Argon2id credential material and reports that no policy upgrade is needed.
Incorrect passwords and malformed verifier material return the same secret-free invalid result without propagating credential-bearing exceptions.
A valid Argon2id encoding below the current approved policy verifies successfully while being marked for replacement with current parameters.

The private login repository normalizes the submitted username and carries the existing account MFA-policy class across the local-account and password-credential persistence boundary without adding schema.
An active local account authenticates through the published Phase 2E Argon2id verifier and emits only stable actor identity, its existing MFA-policy class, and secret-free audit evidence.
Missing accounts, incorrect passwords, and disabled accounts produce the same generic result and secret-free audit shape while each performs one Argon2id verification.
Injected positive account, source, and rolling-window limits are enforced independently with a deterministic clock and no invented production threshold.
A limited request receives the same generic external rejection without account lookup while secret-free internal evidence records that the rate-limit control acted.
The bounded Phase 2F login-security requirements remain mechanically linked to the focused executable tests.
The required/optional policy matrix denies normal actor establishment until required enrollment and every enrolled account's challenge are complete, while allowing optional unenrolled accounts.
An optional unenrolled actor receives no authority from MFA policy and retains only separately provider-established capability grants.
Unknown or inconsistent provider-neutral policy evidence fails closed and records only bounded secret-free decision fields.
Arbitrary invalid MFA policy inputs are replaced by a bounded invalid marker before audit recording so caller-controlled values cannot leak into evidence.
The bounded Phase 2G MFA policy-enforcement requirements remain mechanically linked to focused executable tests.
An injected clock proves browser-session access is allowed before and denied exactly at the fixed 30-minute inactivity boundary.
Recent recorded activity advances only inactivity state and cannot move the fixed authentication timestamp or 24-hour absolute expiry.
Provider-neutral activity updates only the last-activity timestamp while retaining the original authentication timestamp.
Activity on an expired session is denied instead of refreshing or returning modified lifetime state.
Explicit revocation records a provider-neutral timestamp and subsequently denies both evaluation and activity.
Naive, inconsistent, or future session timestamps deny access rather than weakening either fixed lifetime boundary.
Lifetime audit evidence has only fixed operation, outcome, and reason fields and accepts no identifier, token, credential, or caller-controlled text.
The bounded Phase 2H browser-session lifetime requirements remain mechanically linked to focused executable tests without claiming excluded high-risk reauthentication behavior.
The complete provider-neutral account-class matrix grants only Owner recovery of distinct Manager and Staff accounts and denies every other class pairing.
Administrative recovery fails closed when actor and target are the same account because no self-recovery class pairing is granted.
Unknown provider-established actor or target classes deny authorization and are replaced by a bounded invalid audit marker.

Each decision records actor and target references, injected timestamp, correlation reference, sanitized account classes, bounded outcome, and bounded reason without accepting recovery or credential material.
The bounded Phase 2I administrative recovery authorization requirements remain mechanically linked to focused executable tests.

Partial Phase 2K persistence-foundation evidence only: additive set and individual-code rows retain UUID identities, opaque verifier encodings, timestamps, invalidation state, and non-secret provenance.
Partial Phase 2K persistence-foundation evidence only: independently identified verifier rows cannot change identity and one row records consumption without consuming its sibling.
Partial Phase 2K persistence-foundation evidence only: set ownership and identity cannot change, and completed invalidation evidence cannot be rewritten.

Partial Phase 2K persistence-foundation evidence only: deterministic database constraints reject unprotected-shaped, mismatched, blank, or incomplete opaque verifier records without claiming semantic proof of cryptographic non-reversibility or selecting an algorithm.
Partial Phase 2K persistence-foundation evidence only: consumed and invalidated timestamps cannot be recorded without the corresponding actor and non-secret provenance.

Partial Phase 2K persistence-foundation evidence only: runtime may read opaque verifier state and advance bounded lifecycle columns but cannot update verifier material, delete/truncate rows, or execute trigger functions.

Partial Phase 2K persistence-foundation evidence only: the runtime identity can create bounded set and verifier rows, including evaluation of the provider-neutral metadata constraint, without broader table authority.
The additive Phase 2K persistence migration refuses destructive rollback and preserves both recovery-code tables at the reviewed head.

Phase 2K entries claim bounded persistence evidence only; generation, cryptographic selection, plaintext handling, lifecycle-service integration, MFA, rate limiting, session revocation, API, UI, and administrative recovery remain deferred.
Partial Phase 2J lifecycle-foundation evidence only: protected presentation transitions from pending to presented exactly once without returning recovery-code material.
Partial Phase 2J lifecycle-foundation evidence only: an unprotected presentation attempt is rejected and leaves the one-time presentation state unchanged.
Partial Phase 2J lifecycle-foundation evidence only: provider-neutral verification consumes only the independently matching active code and preserves every other verifier lifecycle state.
Partial Phase 2J lifecycle-foundation evidence only: a matching consumed verifier produces a generic outward rejection, preserves a secret-free audit reason, and cannot change lifecycle state.

Partial Phase 2J lifecycle-foundation evidence only: protected regeneration invalidates all old verifier references with per-code state evidence, and subsequent use of an old code is generically rejected.
Partial Phase 2J lifecycle-foundation evidence only: regeneration invalidation requires a protected flow and rejects an unprotected attempt without changing verifier lifecycle state.
Partial Phase 2J lifecycle-foundation evidence only: unknown, empty, or duplicate lifecycle state is rejected before any verifier-provider call.
Partial Phase 2J lifecycle-foundation evidence only: zero or multiple provider matches produce the same generic closed rejection and unchanged state.
Partial Phase 2J lifecycle-foundation evidence only: consumption is unavailable until the protected one-time presentation transition has been recorded.
Partial Phase 2J lifecycle-foundation evidence only: presentation and regeneration reject malformed verifier lifecycle snapshots without repairing or advancing them.
Partial Phase 2J lifecycle-foundation evidence only: verifier-provider failure becomes a generic closed rejection with no candidate material in the result or audit evidence.
Partial Phase 2J lifecycle-foundation evidence only: lifecycle audit evidence has a fixed non-secret shape and excludes candidate code and opaque verifier material.

The implemented Phase 2J tests are bounded partial lifecycle-foundation evidence only; generation, durable verifier storage, endpoint rate limiting/enumeration controls, session revocation, persistence, API, and UI obligations remain explicitly deferred.
Phase 2L provider-foundation evidence: the provider-neutral generator contract requests a fresh fixed 256-bit cryptographic entropy input for every independently usable recovery code.

Phase 2L provider-foundation evidence: the bounded verifier contract returns independently salted Argon2id opaque encodings and metadata compatible with the published provider-neutral persistence columns.
Phase 2L provider-foundation evidence: empty, whitespace-only, and control-bearing code material cannot be encoded as a usable verifier.
Phase 2L provider-foundation evidence: malformed candidates, empty or malformed encodings, and encodings for another provider fail closed without exceptions or secret-bearing output.
Phase 2L provider-foundation evidence: verifier output excludes plaintext and contains only opaque encoding, algorithm, and positive work-factor metadata with no reversible field or operation.
Phase 2L provider-foundation evidence: generated secret material is redacted from representations and generation, encoding, and verification emit no stdout, stderr, or log content.

Phase 2L generation and irreversible-verifier tests remain mechanically linked to the routed authorities without claiming persistence, lifecycle integration, orchestration, API, UI, deployment, or other excluded behavior.
The TEST-117 manifest structure and executable test coverage are validated automatically.
The machine-readable contract names distinct runtime, migration, backup, restore, and exceptional human-administration roles with bounded standing access.
Development, test, staging, and production examples contain only distinct environment-bound protected-file source references.
Deployment-mode validation rejects the production profile until every independently protected source is mounted, without emitting source contents.
Profiles containing direct secret inputs fail validation and rejected values are absent from diagnostics.
Protected-file references containing parent traversal are rejected before any source is resolved.
Backup encryption material has a source class and path distinct from every database credential and ordinary application secret.
Protected server source names are not Vite inputs and do not appear in frontend source.
Local bootstrap reads secret values through environment-backed psql variables, grants backup read and human monitoring only, and leaves restore without standing data access.
The isolated database wrapper keeps its temporary secret directory private while making protected-file mounts readable by the unrelated PostgreSQL container identity on native Linux.
A failed isolated PostgreSQL startup emits container diagnostics before cleanup while redacting every generated identity password.
Real PostgreSQL proves five non-superuser/non-role-creating identities, read-only backup access, and no standing data path for restore or human administration.
Phase 2M composes authorized generation and irreversible encoding into one complete independently identified verifier set before plaintext can cross the one-time caller boundary.
The provider-neutral authorization contract fails closed before generating or persisting any recovery-code material.
An authorization-provider failure is reduced to the same generic pre-generation rejection without exposing provider detail or producing recovery-code material.
Generator or irreversible-verifier failure produces one generic closed outcome and no partial persistence call or secret-bearing exception representation.
Persistence failure closes generically while recording immutable secret-free failure evidence without plaintext or provider detail.
A duplicate generator result cannot produce a set that falsely claims independently usable recovery codes.
The issuance contract rejects a zero-sized set without selecting a product-level recovery-code count.
Blank, whitespace-only, or control-bearing correlation and provenance values are rejected before authorization or secret generation.
A deterministic adapter contract test proves the PostgreSQL boundary prepares the set and opaque verifier writes before exactly one commit; real schema behavior remains covered by make database-test.
A deterministic adapter contract test proves a partial insertion exception rolls back once and never commits; real schema behavior remains covered by make database-test.
Plaintext and opaque verifier values are redacted from representations, plaintext is absent from service state, and issuance emits no log, stdout, or stderr content.
The caller-owned presentation contract removes plaintext on first release and deterministically rejects a second presentation attempt.
The published secure generator and Argon2id provider compose through the provider-neutral issuance contracts and produce independently matching persisted verifiers.

Phase 2M issuance evidence remains mechanically bounded to authorized set creation, one-time plaintext presentation, transaction failure handling, and provider composition without claiming excluded recovery behavior.
Phase 2N composes the published lifecycle and verifier through one atomic persistence call, advances only the independently matching code, and emits no candidate or verifier material.
Consumed and invalidated matching verifiers preserve their lifecycle state and return the same generic outward rejection while retaining bounded secret-free internal evidence.
A persistence exception produces only a generic closed failure and immutable evidence whose fixed values exclude candidate, verifier, and provider detail.
A deterministic adapter contract test verifies exact-set row locking, one guarded lifecycle update, and one commit; real PostgreSQL behavior is claimed only by the dedicated database test.
A guarded update that affects no row fails closed and rolls back rather than reporting or persisting a successful single-use transition.

The atomic PostgreSQL lifecycle update carries secret-free correlation, provenance, reason, and previous/resulting state; a secondary sink failure cannot turn its committed success into a false outward failure.
The dedicated make database-test gate proves against real PostgreSQL that one matching verifier is durably consumed once, reuse is generically rejected, and a sibling verifier remains active.

Phase 2N evidence is mechanically bounded to atomic single-use consumption orchestration and excludes API, UI, account or MFA mutation, session revocation, rate limiting, enumeration handling, regeneration, administrative recovery, and production operations.

Protected authorization, independent replacement generation, atomic prior-set replacement, immutable secret-free evidence, and caller-owned one-time presentation compose through one bounded service call.
Denied protected callers cannot generate replacement secrets or reach persistence and receive only a generic rejection with secret-free evidence.
Authorization-provider failure fails closed before secret generation without exposing provider detail.
Audit-sink unavailability on authorization denial remains a generic fail-closed rejection and cannot permit replacement-secret generation.
Replacement persistence failure returns one generic secret-free failure and relies on the atomic repository boundary to preserve prior durable state.
Audit-sink unavailability after a persistence failure remains one generic closed failure without exposing replacement secrets or internal detail.
Verifier failure returns a generic exception with no cause, context, traceback-local, plaintext, or verifier-material disclosure.
Replacement-set identifier failure remains generic, is audited without an active provider exception, and cannot expose internal detail.
Duplicate generated material is rejected before persistence so a non-independent replacement cannot invalidate the usable prior set.
The published secure generator and Argon2id provider create distinct replacement codes with independently salted matching verifier encodings.
Regeneration rejects empty, padded, or non-printable correlation and provenance context at its protected boundary.
Committed database provenance remains authoritative and a secondary audit-sink failure cannot turn durable regeneration success into a false outward failure.
The deterministic adapter contract locks the exact prior set and persists invalidation provenance, one replacement set, and its verifier rows before one commit.
A verifier-batch failure rolls back the prior-set invalidation and partial replacement rather than committing an unusable recovery state.
Missing and already-invalidated exact prior sets fail closed before any replacement insert, preventing stale repeated regeneration.
The dedicated database gate proves prior-code rejection, immutable invalidation evidence, matching replacement verifiers, and stale-repeat rejection against real PostgreSQL.

Phase 2O evidence is mechanically bounded to protected prior-set invalidation, atomic replacement persistence, independent verifier material, one-time presentation, and secret-free evidence without claiming excluded recovery behavior.
One password-reset trigger revokes every caller-selected applicable immutable session through the published browser-session boundary at one controlled instant.

The orchestration boundary accepts only UUID target and correlation identifiers and rejects free-form, overlong, password-like, API-key-like, or JWT-like values before any session state or audit evidence is produced.
Only password reset, account disablement, and material privilege reduction are accepted; an invented credential-change trigger fails closed.
Audit-sink failure returns one generic closed failure with no internal exception chain and no caller-visible replacement session state.
Revocation cannot proceed without a trustworthy aware timestamp and clock-provider detail never crosses the orchestration boundary.

A second-session browser-boundary failure is translated outside the active provider exception into one generic failure, secret-free failed evidence, and no caller-visible partial revoked-state result.
Each of the three approved account-level triggers produces the exact bounded reason in immutable evidence without broadening revocation policy.
Account-level evidence has a fixed secret-free shape containing target, time, correlation, approved trigger, bounded outcome/reason, and aggregate counts only.

Phase 2P evidence is mechanically bounded to provider-neutral account-trigger orchestration over the published browser-session boundary and excludes API, UI, cookie transport, account or credential mutation, persistence, and production operations.
The service seam returns only the bounded durable closure result supplied by the atomic repository boundary.
The PostgreSQL adapter invokes only the protected closure function with non-secret UUID context and leaves commit or rollback to the enclosing Owner-bootstrap transaction.
Persistence failure crosses the protected service boundary only as a generic unchained failure so the enclosing Owner-bootstrap transaction can roll back atomically.
Missing or malformed database outcomes fail closed without a commit or leaked database detail.
The service boundary accepts only bounded non-secret UUID target and correlation identifiers.
Real PostgreSQL schema inspection limits closure and audit storage to identifiers, timestamp, bounded outcome/reason, correlation, and non-secret state.
The first closure succeeds and a repeated attempt is rejected while both outcomes retain immutable secret-free audit evidence.
The closure primitive does not conflate the separate MFA-policy field with Owner-role authority; the future protected bootstrap composition remains responsible for Owner establishment.
Database triggers reject updates, deletes, and truncation of both the permanent closure marker and its audit history.
The function is a fixed-search-path definer boundary with no PUBLIC or normal-runtime execution grant; the runtime identity also cannot inspect closure or audit rows.
Two concurrent real-PostgreSQL attempts serialize transactionally so exactly one closure succeeds and one rejected attempt is audited.
The forward-only migration refuses destructive downgrade while retaining closure state, audit storage, and the current schema revision.
V1-012 evidence is mechanically bounded to the transactional closure guard, immutable audit persistence, protected service seam, and excluded public API/CLI and secret-handling scope.
Deterministic RFC 6238 Appendix B vectors verify the standards-based SHA-1 TOTP calculation.
Exact-counter verification accepts a correct challenge and fails closed for wrong, stale, or malformed codes without inventing a challenge-window policy.
Enrollment seeds use a fixed 160-bit cryptographic entropy floor and RFC 4648 Base32 provisioning material.
AES-256-GCM encrypts TOTP seeds with actor- and enrollment-bound associated data and explicit key identification.
Authenticated secret protection rejects ciphertext tampering, wrong keys, and invalid AES-256 key material through one generic failure.
Generation, protection, and verification keep plaintext enrollment seeds out of representations, logs, and output streams.
Real PostgreSQL schema inspection verifies encrypted enrollment material, TOTP parameters, lifecycle evidence, and separation from role or capability authority.
Database constraints reject undersized ciphertext, invalid nonces, unbounded key identifiers, unauthenticated protection algorithms, and unsupported TOTP algorithms.
Forward-only pending, active, and disabled transitions preserve verifier provenance and permit only one live enrollment per actor while retaining disabled history.
The runtime identity can read protected verifier material and advance lifecycle columns but cannot update ciphertext, read provenance, delete, truncate, or execute trigger functions directly.
The forward-only migration refuses destructive rollback and retains protected TOTP enrollment state at the reviewed head.
V1-013 evidence is mechanically bounded to RFC 6238 cryptography, authenticated secret protection, persistence, and excludes public API/UI, SMS, production keys, and broader MFA orchestration.
